sound: Checked against the code as it now stands: data boundary (recordsBlock, inert strips angle brackets and brackets), delink of model output, unshown-citation removal, the possible-only drop in TIED sections, the ownStatement and earlierHolder guards, ownWords rewording of 'free' and similar, the quoted fallback paths, and the deadline/hedge/avoid retry. quotedDeepBrief is cited, citations are numbered, numbers are not cut by clipWords, and it does not crash on raw saved r6/r7/r9 reports. The audit items ui-brief-free-word, llm-brief-links-images, llm-prompt-injection-framing and critic-unverified-claimed-role are fixed. llm-brief-namesake-redflag is only partly fixed (see the findings).

findings.title: Model brief can call a failed screen clean: SCREENS and GAPS sections are never checked
findings.scenario: Report where sanctions-lists failed (2 of 2 lookups errored, screen status 'failed'). The model writes '• Sanctions and watchlists: no match in Sanctions lists' and '• Every screen answered in full.' Both lines are kept (mode 'ai'). Its bottom line leaves out the silent screen and passes. GAPS also keeps an uncited '• She was investigated by the FCA for insider trading in 2017.'
findings.fix: Do not take PUBLIC-RECORD SCREENS from the model: always use screenLines(report). In BOTTOM LINE, always add the assembled silent-screens sentence when silentScreens() is not empty. In GAPS, drop an uncited line unless it matches NO_CLAIM or a coverage label.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. With the sanctions screen 'failed', the model's '• Sanctions and watchlists: no match in Sanctions lists' and '• Every screen answered in full.' are kept, because SCREENS and GAPS are outside FACT_SECTIONS. The uncited FCA claim in GAPS is kept too. The bottom line loses the silent-screens sentence, and nothing puts it back.
findings.betterFix: Always set PUBLIC-RECORD SCREENS to screenLines(report), ignoring the model. Append the assembled silent-screens sentence to BOTTOM LINE whenever silentScreens() is not empty and the kept text does not name each label. In GAPS, keep an uncited line only if it matches an anchored NO_CLAIM or names a coverage or screen label.

findings.title: Name-only or invented red flags pass by adding one tied citation; the overlap test needs one 5-letter stem
findings.scenario: Reproduced, all kept in mode 'ai': (a) RED FLAGS '• Arrested for burglary in Leeds in 2018 [Source 3 (possible)] [Source 2 (tied bio)]'. ns.some(tied) passes, and sharesWords matches against the namesake record itself. (b) '• Sued by Acme Bank for embezzlement in 2018 [Source 2]' passes because the bio mentions 'Acme'. (c) BOTTOM LINE 'She was convicted of embezzlement at Acme Bank in 2015 [Source 2]' gets no content check at all.
findings.fix: In RED FLAGS, compute sharesWords only over tied, non-ownStatement cited records, and drop the possible citations from the line. Require at least two distinctive stems, including one event word (charged, sued, convicted, fined and similar) present in the record. Run the same check on BOTTOM LINE sentences that carry event words.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced in mode 'ai'. With a name-only record (n4) in sections, '• Arrested for burglary in Leeds [Source 4] [Source 2]' is kept: tied() passes on the bio, and sharesWords matches the namesake's own words. 'Sued by Acme Bank…[Source 2]' is kept on 'acme'. A bottom-line 'convicted of embezzlement…[Source 2]' gets no content check.
findings.betterFix: In RED FLAGS and in bottom-line sentences that hold event words, strip the possible and assumedTie citations first, then run sharesWords only over the remaining tied records that are not ownStatement. Require that a record also holds an event stem (charg/sued/convi/fined/arres/indic/settl…) and one other distinctive stem. If that fails, drop the unit.

findings.title: Uncited accusations pass the fact-section check through the NO_CLAIM and LABEL escapes
findings.scenario: In RED FLAGS, '• Convicted of embezzlement in 2015; no records of an appeal were found.' is kept with no citation, because NO_CLAIM matches 'no records' anywhere in the line. In BOTTOM LINE, 'Convicted of wire fraud in Ohio in 2016:' is kept because it fits LABEL (short text ending in a colon).
findings.fix: Anchor NO_CLAIM to the whole line (e.g. ^[•\s]*(?:None found|No ... found)\b[^;]*$) and reject a line holding an event word. Allow LABEL only outside BOTTOM LINE, and only for the known labels ('About the company:', 'To confirm with the person:', 'Only if this is the right person').
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. '• Convicted of embezzlement in 2015; no records of an appeal were found.' is kept uncited in RED FLAGS, because NO_CLAIM is unanchored. The LABEL escape needs a bottom-line sentence that ends in a colon. That is narrower than claimed, but the regex allows it.
findings.betterFix: Make NO_CLAIM match the whole unit (anchored, and no event stem anywhere in it). Allow LABEL only outside BOTTOM LINE, and only for the known labels ('About the company', 'To confirm with the person', 'Only if this is the right person').

findings.title: Matters that hold only if this is the right person are silently dropped from the AI brief
findings.scenario: No company typed; ifRightPerson holds 'Jane Roe of Zeta sued for fraud by investors' (assumedTie). The model follows the prompt and writes it under RED FLAGS after 'Only if this is the right person:', plus one bottom-line sentence. keepUnit drops both, because tied() excludes assumedTie. The AI brief is accepted with RED FLAGS reading 'None found… Only if this is the right person:' and nothing under it.
findings.fix: In RED FLAGS, accept assumedTie citations for lines that follow an 'Only if this is the right person' label, and say so in the prompt. Or, when report.ifRightPerson is not empty, always add the assembled ifRightPerson block and its bottom-line sentence to the AI brief.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. The model writes the assumedTie matter under 'Only if this is the right person:' as the prompt asks, and keepUnit drops it because tied() excludes assumedTie. The AI brief is accepted with a dangling label and nothing under it. The assembled ifRightPerson block is never put back.
findings.betterFix: After the checks, replace the model's 'Only if this is the right person' block with the assembled one whenever report.ifRightPerson is not empty. Keep the assembled bottom-line sentence that counts these matters. Do not loosen tied() for other lines.

findings.title: Fraud amounts, valuations and stock values shown as 'latest funding'; an SEC charge release shown as a filing that 'confirms' a funding round
findings.scenario: Rebuilt Trevor Milton r9: BOTTOM LINE says 'the latest funding on record is $600M (2023-12-18) [72]', where 72 is NY Post '…four years in prison for $600M fraud'. WHAT CHECKS OUT says 'An SEC filing confirms Nikola's funding round: $1 billion' citing SEC press release 'SEC Charges Founder of Nikola Corp. With Fraud'. Jack Zhang's brief gives '$15.9 billion' as the latest round. Root cause: round-less amounts from companyFacts.js.
findings.fix: In the brief, state a funding entry as a round only when it has a round label or comes from a Form D (data.form==='D'). In whatChecksOut, require the cited record to be an offering filing whose quote contains the amount. officialKind should call SEC press releases 'an SEC press release'. Also fix the amount extraction in companyFacts.js.
findings.verifyNote: Rebuilt from r9 with the current buildCompanyFacts. Nikola's funding shows $600M from 'gets four years in prison for $600M fraud' (RAISE matches 'gets'), $3.1B from a stock-forfeit headline and $1 billion from an SEC charge release plus Milton's new AI-plane raise. WHAT CHECKS OUT says 'An SEC filing confirms Nikola's funding round: $1 billion'. Zhang's round shows $15.9B.
findings.betterFix: In companyFacts, drop round-less amounts unless the sentence holds a funding noun (funding, round, financing, investment) and no crime, fine or settlement word, and drop 'gets'/'got' from RAISE. In whatChecksOut, confirm funding only from a Form D whose quote holds the amount. In officialKind, call an SEC press release 'an SEC press release'.

findings.title: COMPANY section prints page navigation text and undated, conflicting valuation headlines
findings.scenario: Jack Zhang r9 COMPANY bullet: '…amid $11 billion valuation Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer Help using this website - Accessibility statement Today's Paper…'. Eric Glyman r9 lists four valuations ($60B, $44B, $30B+, $32B) as raw headlines, two of them ending ' - CNBC.' / ' - saastr.com.'. They are undated and unordered, so the reader cannot tell which is current.
findings.fix: Filter standing text that holds site-chrome phrases (skip to, accessibility statement, today's paper, cookie, sign in). Render standing as kind, value and the cited record's date, newest first, and strip a trailing ' - Publisher'. Fix clipAround in companyFacts.js too.
findings.verifyNote: Rebuilt Zhang COMPANY: '…amid $11 billion valuation Skip to navigation Skip to content … Today's Paper…'. Glyman shows four valuation headlines, two ending ' - CNBC.' and ' - saastr.com.'. reportCompanyFacts drops the standing date, so the brief cannot order or date them.
findings.betterFix: Keep kind, value and date in reportCompanyFacts. In companyFacts, cut sentences at site-chrome phrases and strip a trailing ' - Publisher'. In the brief, show one line per kind (the newest value with its date), the others as earlier figures.

findings.title: COMPANY lists a domain that an earlier holder registered as the company's web domain
findings.scenario: Trevor Milton r9: COMPANY shows '• Web domains: trevormilton.com [Source 171]'. Record 171 has data.earlierHolder true and the title 'first registered 2007-01-24, by an earlier holder (Nikola was founded in 2015)'. whatChecksOut excludes earlierHolder records, but the COMPANY line does not.
findings.fix: In assembleSections' company list, keep a domain only when at least one cited record has no data.earlierHolder (use byN). Apply the same filter in companyFacts.js.
findings.verifyNote: companyNames adds every non-possible domain-history record. earlierHolder is set only in buildReport's mapping, after the facts are built. So the rebuilt Milton COMPANY lists 'Web domains: trevormilton.com' (registered 2007; Nikola was founded in 2015), which is his personal domain, not the company's.
findings.betterFix: In assembleSections, keep a domain only when one cited record (byN) is not earlierHolder. Better still, pass the founded year into companyNames and skip domains registered more than a year before it.

findings.title: Bottom line names the most serious matter without its latest outcome (Milton's pardon is missing)
findings.scenario: Trevor Milton r9: the bottom line reads 'the most serious: Trevor Milton Sentenced To Four Years In Prison… (2023-12-18)'. The 2025 presidential pardon (red flag 8, record 10) is never connected to it. Even when f.outcome exists (a dismissed suit, for example), line 1620 omits it, although the prompt asks for the latest outcome.
findings.fix: Add '; latest outcome: …' from flags[0].outcome to the bottom-line sentence, as flagLine does. Upstream, attach pardon, acquittal and dismissal records as outcomes to the matter they resolve (report owner).
findings.verifyNote: Line 1620 never reads flags[0].outcome, while flagLine does, so the bottom line states the most serious matter without its outcome even when a record gives one. The Milton pardon gap is mainly upstream: no outcome is attached to his flags.
findings.betterFix: Reuse flagLine's outcome fragment in the bottom-line sentence. Separately, in report.js, attach pardon, acquittal, dismissal and vacated records as the outcome of the matter they resolve, by matterKey or docket.

findings.title: Founder questions ask about third-party press rewrites, and ask for 'court documents' for press pieces
findings.scenario: Questions produced: 'Ask what changed and why: cnbc.com page: bio rewritten between 2025-03 and 2026-01' (Milton), 'fortune.com page…' (Glyman) and 'clay.com…' (Zhang). Jack Zhang also gets 'Ask for… its final court or regulator documents: Career, as told on afr.com: …defies US attacks'. Milton's three redFlag questions all concern the same case, using up slots.
findings.fix: Build change questions only from claimChanges with field in (title, role, dates, headline) or on the person's own pages. Use the court/regulator wording only for official-record or litigation/regulatory flags, and a 'what is your account of…' wording for press. Merge questions for the same matterKey.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. 'Ask what changed and why: cnbc.com page: bio rewritten…' (Milton) and 'clay.com page' (Zhang). Zhang gets 'final court or regulator documents' for an afr.com career article. Milton's three redFlag questions cover one prosecution.
findings.betterFix: Build change questions only from title, role or date changes, or from the person's own pages. Use the court-documents wording only for official litigation or regulatory flags, and ask for their account otherwise. Group redFlags by matterKey before taking three. Also fix upstream why 'Career, as told on…' records become red flags.
